links.outcome: Prospective accuracy of the RF model on a second-batch cohort, evaluated by AUROC
links.effect: Prospective cohort of 74 individuals gave AUROC 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD.
links.quote: The 295 cases collected in the first batch were used for model development and software creation, and the developed model was then evaluated in a prospective cohort of 74 individuals in the second batch, achieving AUROC values of 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for predicting no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Cost-effectiveness comparison of AI-based screening at a suburban hospital versus a tertiary specialty clinic
AI-based screening for NAFLD in primary care

screen.reason: The study deploys a machine-learning-based NAFLD screening platform in a real-world community hospital health check-up workflow and evaluates its diagnostic yield and cost-effectiveness, but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or guardrail.
